Head east or to the Pyrenees for affordable mountain resorts offering a rich cultural experience. By Abigail Butcher Last updated December 15, 2025 • 8 min read This story is created by National Geographic Traveller (UK). As options for the traditional chalet ski break have dwindled and prices risen, venturing to Europe’s far corners and beyond for a ski break can reap rewards. Costs are often lower, while luxury accommodation can be similarly priced to budget options in mainstream European ski resorts. As well as being potentially cheaper, skiing in territory off the beaten track can offer a rich cultural experience, plus better flight routes, less crowded slopes, sunnier days and a friendlier welcome. 1. The Pyrenees Stretching more than 430km from southwestern France all the way to northwest Spain — with Andorra in their heart — the Pyrenees are home to dozens of ski resorts big and small. Standouts include Baqueira-Beret in Spain, Soldeu in Andorra and Grand Tourmalet in France — and all are known for being cheaper than the Alps and often snowier, thanks to their Atlantic-maritime climate. pages.text: Billions of T. rex likely roamed the Earth, paleontologists report | National Geographic Paleontologists figured out how many T. rex lived on Earth—and they found that about 20,000 would have been alive at any given time during a two- to three-million year timespan. Illustration by STOCKTREK IMAGES, Nat Geo Image Collection SCIENCE NEWS Billions of T. rex likely roamed the Earth, paleontologists report The iconic predator’s estimated abundance means the T. rex fossils we have today are exceedingly rare. By Michael Greshko Published April 19, 2021 • 6 min read If you traveled back in time 67 million years ago to ancient Montana, you’d be entering the realm of a tyrant: the iconic predator Tyrannosaurus rex . Before you venture into that lost world, though, you might want to know: On average, how close is the nearest T. rex to you? That might sound like an impossible thing to know—but after crunching through two decades’ worth of T. rex research, a new study provides estimates of the animal’s population density. In all likelihood, a T. rex would be within 15 miles of you, if not much closer. The new study, published last Thursday in Science , also translates these population densities into estimates for how many T. rex ever lived. On average, researchers estimate that some 20,000 T. rex lived at any one time and that about 127,000 generations of the dinosaurs lived and died. Those averages imply that a total of 2.5 billion T. rex lived in the species’ native North America, possibly as far north as Alaska and as far south as Mexico, over a two- to three-million-year timespan.

And yet we know little about their movements and intentions, mostly because this ethereal world has largely been inaccessible for research. But new technologies are providing a window into how animals use their aerial habitat to travel and hunt. The burgeoning field is called “aeroecology,” and researchers are revealing just how substantially humans are altering the world overhead—with deadly consequences for flying animals. The new insights are giving us ways to make the air safer for these creatures. In this episode, host Ari Daniel speaks with Dustin Partridge of the New York City Bird Alliance as he directs the intermittent shutdown of the iconic Tribute in Light to protect disoriented birds during 9/11 this year. Once numbering ~30 million and ranging across the United States and in Canada and Mexico, bison were hunted to near extinction, with only several hundred remaining by the 1870’s. pages.description: Scott Colom is the first black man to sit in the Senate for Mississippi in 145 years.
pages.text: Black Mississippians celebrate a victory almost no one saw coming Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Black Mississippians celebrate a victory almost no one saw coming 5 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Brandon Drenon Jackson, Mississippi BBC/ Brandon Drenon The NAACP helped get people out to vote, knocking on more than twice as many doors this election than last The scene was 145 years in the making. Dozens of people filled a tiny room inside the historic Masonic Lodge Hall in Jackson, Mississippi, on Wednesday, waiting to hear whether Scott Colom would become the state's next US Senator. The 70-year-old building is the permanent residence of the NAACP's state headquarters, where civil rights leaders, many of them there that night, worked for decades to create this moment. When a large speaker blared the news of Colom's win, it ended a long, anxious wait for results that came over a week after election day. The room exploded with emotion. "Yes sir," one man yelled, dropping to the ground and moving his arms and legs as if to make a snow angel on the carpet floor. Colom's victory is the first win for Democrats in that seat in 40 years. It is also the first time a black politician held the seat since 1881. Through collaborative efforts, state and local entities that provide employment support services can maximize employment and economic advancement outcomes for disabled people. Blending, braiding, and sequencing (BBS) are innovative strategies that maximize the efficient and effective use of federal funds across systems to help people with disabilities secure and maintain CIE. Defining BBS Blending occurs when dollars from multiple funding streams combine to create a single “pot” of commingled dollars that can fund an initiative or purchase more specific services. Blending involves pooling funds from multiple sources to support a common goal, such that each individual funding source gives up its program identity. Typically, states or regions need explicit authorization by statute or regulation to allow the blending of funds. Effective Nov. 1, 2025, the camping limit at Mittry Lake will change from 10 days per calendar year to 14 days within a 28-day period . ELY, Nev. – The Bureau of Land Management began a wild horse gather Nov. 14, in and around the Antelope Complex Herd Management Area in northern Nevada, to protect the health of the herd as late season forage declines and winter approaches. The gather will help reduce the risks wild horses face when the range can no longer support the current population. The Antelope Complex includes the Antelope, Antelope Valley, Goshute, and Spruce-Pequop Herd Management Areas. Horses may appear healthy at the start of the fall, but forage and water resources are limited. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn BLM Fishing Derby brings Americans Outside for recreation and stewardship in Imperial Valley, California Oct 13, 2026 In a region best known for its off-highway vehicle adventures, the BLM California's El Centro Field Office hooked a different type of recreator for its second annual Fishing Derby Cast and Clean-up event. More than 100 members of the local community gathered for the event on Saturday, Sept. 26, bringing together recreation, community engagement, and public-land stewardship on BLM-managed public lands in Imperial County, California. The fishing derby took place at the Hot Springs Long-Term Visitor Area and on BLM-managed lands adjacent to the Highline and All-American canals. For many attendees, it was their first fishing opportunity, and several first-time anglers caught their first fish. Reducing vegetation along roads can create a break in fuels, giving firefighters another option if conditions change. Crews removed vegetation within approximately 75 feet of the roadside to create a potential firebreak if the fire moved in that direction. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/blockchain Information technology Blockchain Sign Up to Get NIST News GovDelivery Blockchain technology provides a way for a community of participants to maintain a shared, tamper-evident, and tamper-resistant digital ledger. It is the underlying technology for many cryptocurrency systems, but it can also be used in other types of applications. A blockchain is the ledger itself. It contains transactional records that are grouped into blocks. Each block is cryptographically linked to the previous block, making the ledger tamper evident. If data in an earlier block is changed, the cryptographic link to that block changes, and the change can be detected in later blocks. As new blocks are added, older blocks become more difficult to modify, creating tamper resistance. A blockchain network is the network in which a blockchain is used. Copies of the ledger are maintained across nodes in the network, and new blocks are added according to established validation and consensus rules. This distributed structure, together with cryptographic mechanisms, helps make the blockchain resilient to later attempts to alter the ledger. Initially dedicated to grumbles, the show's unique format was soon expanded to include praise. Speaking at Monday's unveiling, Praise or Grumble's longest-running presenter Andy Giddings said: "It's not about who sits in the chair, it's about the people who get involved. The inhabitants of San Juan aren’t early risers. At 9am, the city’s streets are largely empty. In the Plaza Colón, there’s a cockerel scrabbling about in the flower beds. A kiosk selling coffee and empanadas is untroubled by customers. “We like a slow start,” Laura Ortiz-Villamil confirms as we sit in the shade, the sun already blazing. In front of us is a statue of Christopher Columbus, a crucifix raised in his left hand. Among the first Europeans to barrel over the Atlantic, all eager to get their hands on whatever land they could, he ‘discovered’ Puerto Rico in 1493 and immediately claimed it for Spain. “The Spanish called it Puerto Rico — rich port — wrongly believing there was gold here,” Laura says as we set off on a stroll around the capital’s historic district, Old San Juan. A born-and-bred Puerto Rican, with tattoos on her arms ranging from Gabriel García Márquez quotes to Peanuts characters, historian Laura set up her guiding company in 2022 to share her country’s “less-known stories, good or bad”. We wander cobbled streets flanked by houses with arched wooden doorways and overhanging balconies, painted in every colour you might think of: pistachio, peach, lemon, spearmint. Close booktiger's Diary [转载]可不能“随手一标”！ Posted by booktiger on 17 October 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . 可不能“随手一标”！ 来源：国家安全部 2026年10月17日07:03 北京 https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/Xri2QFc-6VPpZ6QLBaqjgw 一张看似普通的网络地图，一个出于“兴趣”的随手标注，竟可能危害国家秘密安全。近年来，随着地理信息技术的普及，“开放地图”平台逐渐走入公众视野，但其背后隐藏的国家安全风险却不容忽视。 一个“爱好”带来的麻烦 2021年，许某在社交媒体上被一张带有艺术风格的路网地图所吸引。出于好奇，他开始接触境外开放地图平台，并违法“翻墙”访问。许某凭借对居住地周边环境的了解，以及从互联网搜集的公开信息，开始在境外开放地图平台上标注各类地理信息，多次标注军队等涉密敏感单位的位置信息。国家安全机关发现许某违法行为后迅速采取行动，依法对其开展审查。面对审查，许某懊悔道：“我完全没想到，自己只是出于爱好做点标记，竟会触犯法律，威胁国家安全。”国家安全机关向其宣讲了相关法律法规，讲明了其行为的危害性，并依法对其进行处理。许某表示已深刻认识到错误，并积极配合消除隐患。 随手一标，隐患巨大 “开放地图”一般指数据开源、可自由使用与编辑的地图项目，经常由全球志愿者共同创建、编辑并免费共享地理数据，在碳中和、城乡交通建设、灾害风险评估研究等方面具备相应应用价值。但如果在开放地图平台上标注我国涉密敏感地理信息，就有可能被不法分子利用，对我国家安全造成危害。不法分子无需动用复杂的技术手段，仅凭开放地图便能轻易获取我国涉密敏感单位的位置、规模等信息，并据此在军事基地等涉密敏感单位附近开展“黑飞”、偷拍、测绘等活动。境外间谍情报机关还可能结合其他渠道获取的信息进行多源数据交叉比对，拼凑成完整情报，甚至还可能对涉密单位工作人员以及周边居民、商户等人员开展针对性的渗透、拉拢和策反活动，对我国家安全构成严重威胁。 国家安全机关提示 《 中华人民共和国保守国家秘密法 》《 中华人民共和国测绘法 》《 公开地图内容表示规范 》等法律法规划出清晰底线：个人或者组织非法获取、持有、提供、利用属于国家秘密的地理信息的，将被依法追责。开放地图不是个人兴趣的“涂鸦板”，看似无心的标注可能触碰国家秘密“红线”。 ——绷紧“安全弦”。增强国家安全意识，不在地图平台标注任何涉及军事基地、涉密单位的地理信息。 ——把好“出口关”。不在社交平台发布涉密场所周边照片、视频，拍照前留意背景是否涉及敏感场所，不转发、不扩散任何标注有涉密地理信息的地图内容。 ——当好“守护者”。如发现在公开地图标注涉密地理信息等危害国家安全的可疑情况，请及时通过12339国家安全机关举报受理电话、网络举报受理平台（ www.12339.gov.cn ）、国家安全部微信公众号举报受理渠道或者直接向当地国家安全机关进行举报。 Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

About Boots to Business Boots to Business (B2B) is an entrepreneurial education and training program offered by SBA as part of the Department of Defense’s Transition Assistance Program (TAP). B2B provides participants with an overview of business ownership and is open to service members (including National Guard and Reserve) and military spouses. What’s your transition mission? Begin your journey Introduction to Entrepreneurship: The foundational two-day, in-person course provides you with an introductory understanding of business ownership. Continue your journey Optional Follow-on Courses: “B2B: Revenue Readiness” is an online course delivered through a partnership with Mississippi State University. Receive sign-up information once you complete the in-person introductory course. B2B and B2BR participants are also encouraged to take advantage of the many resources offered by the SBA and its partner network. Home » SBA leadership » Brad Zaun Download high-resolution image Brad Zaun Regional Administrator Brad Zaun is the Great Plains Regional Administrator serving Iowa, Kansas, Missouri and Nebraska. He leverages over two decades of experience as a dedicated small business owner, community leader, and public servant. As former owner/operator of Zaun’s Trustworthy Hardware and vice president of R and R Realty Marketing Group, he gained direct insight into the complexities and needs of entrepreneurs. Mr. Zaun’s extensive public service includes terms on the City Council of Urbandale, Iowa, and as mayor from 1998 to 2004, followed by 20 years championing small businesses in the Iowa State Senate from 2005 to 2025.
